clue.text: Unsubtle spy?

definitions.meaning: plain-spoken and tactless, saying things without tact
Anthony ..., the art historian exposed as a Soviet spy in the Cambridge Five

explanation.surface: A question about whether a clumsy, obvious agent can really be called a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: Anthony Blunt, Surveyor of the Queen's Pictures, was one of the Cambridge spy ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank speech with no tact is called this; the second sense is the surname of a famous British traitor.

clue.text: Sexed-up story of waistcoat on murderer

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a bodice was historically a kind of waistcoat or close-fitting upper garment
a ripper is a killer, as in Jack the Ripper

explanation.surface: A racy tale about a vest found on a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places BODICE above RIPPER in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamy historical romance novel, typically with heaving bosoms on the cover.

clue.text: Such a rule never makes it into the law books

definitions.text: Such a rule never makes it into the law books

parts.words: Such a rule never makes it into the law books
parts.note: a convention understood by everyone but never formally recorded as law

explanation.surface: A rule that is never actually recorded among statutes.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an 'unwritten rule': a custom everyone follows though nothing sets it down.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs observed without formal record are described as never set down on paper.

clue.text: Asian dog covers miles

indicators.note: the follow word covers, enclosing the miles letter

parts.note: to dog someone is to tail or follow them

explanation.surface: An Asian dog breed that covers long distances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is a verb meaning follow, giving TAIL; 'covers' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A people of southern India and Sri Lanka, so a person from Asia.

clue.text: Cost to keep part of play in rehearsal

indicators.note: the cost word holds the stage section within it, as a box keeps its contents

parts.note: the cost of something is its price
a play is divided into acts

explanation.surface: Theatre budgeting: keeping one section of a play affordable during rehearsals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of play' looks like a selection signal, but it is a whole unit: a play is divided into numbered sections.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated exercise to improve a performance; synonym for going over lines before a show.

clue.text: Works out questions, really hard

parts.note: to pump someone is to question them persistently
iron as an adjective means extremely hard or unyielding

explanation.surface: Someone thinks hard to solve problems, really grinding at them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works out' looks like solving, but it is gym exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting weights in a gym is exercising, an idiom for training the muscles.

clue.text: Essentially sacred ground

indicators.note: the essence of the word sits at its core, so the inner letters are kept

explanation.surface: Holy land at its very core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' takes SACRED without its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of land area, so a piece of ground.

clue.text: Distinguished, but not given full information?

definitions.meaning: recognised as different from one another
read whimsically as informed of only a portion

explanation.surface: Someone eminent who is nonetheless kept partly in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: someone informed of just a fragment of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able to separate two similar things; the cryptic second half means having heard only a fragment.

clue.text: It's blown out of the water

definitions.text: It's blown out of the water

parts.words: It's blown out of the water
parts.note: a large seashell, taken from the sea, that is sounded like a horn

explanation.walkthrough: 'blown out of the water' suggests utter defeat, but the shell is literally blown, as a trumpet, after being taken from the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral seashell used as a trumpet, as in Lord of the Flies.

clue.text: Many older women stray this nostalgic way

indicators.note: to stray is to wander off course, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A wistful scene of elderly ladies wandering off along a memory-filled path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stray' signals the anagram of all fourteen letters of MANY OLDER WOMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for indulging in reminiscence, pictured as a road back through the past.

clue.text: To look for gold entails outline plans

parts.note: to prospect is to search the ground for gold or minerals
something that entails a thing needs it, that is, uses it

explanation.surface: Gold-hunting involves drawing up rough plans.
explanation.definitionFit: Documents setting out a scheme or offer for investors are outlines of plans.

clue.text: Upper-class type may be such a wonder

definitions.text: Upper-class type may be such a wonder

parts.words: Upper-class type may be such a wonder
parts.note: completes the British phrase for a feeble, ineffectual aristocrat, mocked for a weak jawline

explanation.surface: Musing that a posh person might turn out to be some kind of marvel.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'chinless wonder' is British slang for a dim, weak-willed upper-class man; 'wonder' looks like praise but is part of the insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a prominent jaw, taken as a sign of a weak character, in the stock phrase for a useless toff.

clue.text: Obese woman priest

parts.note: obese means very fat
her is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A curt description pairing a heavy woman with a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woman' gives the pronoun HER, a common crossword move.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic and Anglican clergy are addressed by this title, so it stands for a priest.

clue.text: Unpleasant argument in Hyde Park?

definitions.note: a definition by location: a place found in the London park

parts.note: rotten means nasty or unpleasant
a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a nasty quarrel broke out in a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: ROTTEN ROW is a historic riding track along the south side of Hyde Park in London; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous sandy horse-riding avenue lies within that royal park in central London.

clue.text: Newspaper editor forced out

parts.note: the Daily Express is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor ousted from the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The Express is a British national daily paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeezed or pressed out, as juice or milk is extracted by pressure.

clue.text: Vital fluid spilled, a decisive juncture

parts.note: water is the fluid all life needs
shed means spilled, as blood or tears are shed

explanation.surface: Some precious liquid spills at a crucial moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vital fluid' looks like blood, but here it is the other essential liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A turning point, from the ridge dividing river basins where rainfall goes one way or the other.

clue.text: Finally short of time for picture book

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: Someone at last short of time to pick out an illustrated book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' removes the final T from AT LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound collection of maps is a book made mostly of pictures.

clue.text: Moving, these animals could be noiseless

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift position into a new order

explanation.surface: Animals that can stalk prey in silence while on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' signals the anagram of NOISELESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Female big cats, the hunters of the pride, are animals described as moving silently.

clue.text: Attractive person to put on board

definitions.meaning: a glamorous figure whose poster is stuck on a wall
to fix a notice to a noticeboard with a drawing pin

explanation.surface: A short instruction to stick a picture of a good-looking person on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a pin-up poster star; the verb phrase is literally fixing something up with a pin.

clue.text: Sick Ottoman — he is refusing visitors

indicators.note: something sick is out of sorts, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A Turkish man, unwell, has shut his door to callers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick' signals the anagram of OTTOMAN HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A householder who declines to receive callers is said, by polite fiction, to be away.

clue.text: Attacked with acid

parts.note: describes an engraver's method of eating lines into a metal plate with corrosive

explanation.walkthrough: 'Attacked' suggests violence, but the corrosion is a printmaking technique on copper plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Engraving by letting a corrosive bite lines into metal is this craft process.

clue.text: Long for clubs to go wild

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit
to rave is to rant or behave wildly

explanation.surface: Yearning for nightclubs where people go wild.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn or hanker after something with intense desire.

clue.text: Wing patterns are extraordinary

indicators.note: letters that are out of the ordinary are not in their usual order

explanation.surface: Butterfly or bird wing markings being remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are extraordinary' signals the anagram of PATTERNS; 'Wing' is an architectural term here, not a bird's.
explanation.definitionFit: Each arm of a cross-shaped church projecting from the nave is a wing of the building.

clue.text: Up in map-reading

parts.note: on a conventional map, the top edge points toward one compass direction

explanation.walkthrough: On a standard map the top of the sheet is this compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Maps are conventionally drawn with this compass point at the top of the sheet.

clue.text: Safari covers a long distance

indicators.note: the word Safari covers the answer, holding it inside its letters

explanation.surface: A safari trip covers many miles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' shows the answer sitting within SAFARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Means at or to a great distance, as in seen from far away.

clue.text: Thorny issues in this conflict?

parts.note: a 15th-century English civil war named after flowers with prickly stems, so its disputes were literally thorny

explanation.surface: A question about the tricky matters at the heart of some war.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lancastrian and Yorkist dynastic war took its name from the red and white rose badges; 'Thorny' is the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval English dynastic civil war is named after the flower badges of the two houses.

clue.text: Translated "plastered"

definitions.meaning: a wall coated with a first layer of plaster or cement

explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' in quotes suggests drunk, but it is the builder's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A text turned into another language and a wall coated with plaster share the same past participle.

clue.text: Welcomes huge numbers

definitions.meaning: receives guests as a party giver
great multitudes, as in heavenly armies

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means receiving guests; the plural noun means vast crowds or multitudes.
